newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch chemical sector sees modest upturn in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dutch chemical sector sees modest upturn in 1997.

text.p: First quarter results in the Dutch chemical sector indicate a modest industry upturn in 1997, sector association VNCI said on Wednesday.
"Based on the first quarter we expect a one percent increase in (selling) prices and a three percent increase in volumes," VNCI chairman Rudy van der Meer told a news conference.
He said turnover in the industry was seen increasing four percent year-on-year to 51.4 billion guilders from a year-earlier 49.4 billion.
The outlook has improved since last December, when VNCI forecast stable prices and slightly higher production volumes.
But Van der Meer said Europe had not contributed to the upturn, as European demand remained stagnant.
"Although the industry outlook is brighter than it was at the end of 1996, the improvement...is due exclusively to increased world demand," he said.
Dutch chemical producers were profiting from world market expansion which had created more room for European products as the U.S. industry struggled to keep pace with demand.
In addition the Dutch had profited from the continued strength of the dollar against the guilder, he said.
Van der Meer said that while the picture for the first half of 1997 was more or less established, the second six months was subject to major uncertainties.
Influential and uncertain factors included future trends in the U.S. economy and development of global chemicals demand, he said.
"China is a major uncertainty (as regards global market demand)," he said, referring to China's unexpected decision in 1995 to suspend polymers buying for some six months.
"That decision closed off a significant market, good for some 30 percent of (world) polymers production," he noted.
It also remained to be seen whether the dollar would continue its current strength against the guilder, Van der Meer added.
